sn28.10:1.4: We don’t meet her elsewhere. Her name appears to mean “fair-face”, but it may be a misspelling of _sūcimukhī_, “needle-mouth”, used elsewhere of mosquitoes or similar creatures ([mn130:20.3](), Atharva Veda 11.10.3). Bold women were a feature of the ascetic communities, as shown by Bhaddā of the Curly Hair ([thig5.9]()) or Gārgī Vācaknavī (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.6.1).
sn28.10:2.1: Her questions are deliberately obscure, a test for the supposedly wise Sāriputta. I haven’t found any references for the ideas here. But to “eat” is is both to “enjoy” and to “nourish”. Her question is about right livelihood. Compare the “six directions” of [dn31]().
sn28.10:4.2: Sāriputta answers the riddle in a way that is simultaneously literal and meaningful. He doesn’t buy into the game of trying to out-riddle the riddler.
